label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: logs COMPLETE, timings COMPLETE, handler max 1610.06 ms, failures 0

report.summary: Notification publication fell to ~1/5 of the arrival rate for about 70 s, then caught up. The consumer handler was slow (p95 ~1.6 s) while LedgerCore, the DB and the pool were healthy. The cause of the slow handler is unconfirmed.

findings.claim: Outbox publications lagged arrivals for ~70 s (about 6 per 10 s vs 28 arriving), then a burst of 70-81 per 10 s drained the backlog.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts show the dip and catch-up; pending peaked at 136 and returned to 2.

findings.claim: Delivery latency comes from the consumer handler, not auth or LedgerCore overhead: handler p95 1605 ms vs p50 0.012 ms, while auth p95 is 74 ms.
findings.reason: Total p95 1677 ms is almost entirely consumer handler time; unattributed time is about 1 ms.

findings.claim: The slow handler probably throttled the outbox poller (batch 20, 1 s poll), delaying notifications. This would fit the dip, but timing was not correlated per attempt.
findings.reason: Attempts that take ~1.6 s each would reduce delivery throughput; the 3 s delivery timeout was not hit and all 418 attempts succeeded.

findings.claim: Transfer API, DB pool and DB locks are healthy and do not explain the delay.
findings.reason: No 5xx, p99 0.25 s, no pool pending or timeouts, and no blocking in any sample.

limitations: The consumer is a test fixture, and there is no evidence on why its handler was slow for some requests.
Per-attempt timestamps were not aligned to the dip buckets, and only 100 of 418 log rows were listed.
next_checks: Correlate per-attempt handler time with the 04:02-04:03:10 dip window to confirm that slow attempts coincide with it.
Inspect the consumer for the cause of ~1.6 s handler stalls, and check the 571 old FAILED rows separately.

alternatives.reason: Failed stayed constant at 571 and the age grows linearly, so it predates the window; it does not explain the dip within it.
alternatives.hypothesis: A stuck FAILED outbox row (oldest undelivered age ~37,000 s, failed=571) is the cause of the late notifications.

alternatives.reason: The pool had no pending borrowers or timeouts, and no blocking was sampled.
alternatives.hypothesis: Database or pool contention slowed the poller.
